title: eSports Management
desc: Plan and run a small eSports team, club or tournament: roster, schedule, wellbeing, fair play, finance and sponsors.
outcomes: Explain how eSports teams and events work.
Judge wellbeing, fair play and contracts.
task: Plan and run a one-day small tournament or a one-month team season, with roster, rules, wellbeing plan, budget and report.
condition: A game with free play, a computer or consoles, a spreadsheet, two peers and a mentor.
standard: Rules are published; fair-play and anti-cheat steps are used; wellbeing plan limits hours and includes breaks; budget totals correct; report with results; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Club leaders, coaches, event organisers, students.
evidence: roster, rules, schedule, wellbeing plan, budget, report
modules: Know the players, teams, publishers and events.
Roles: player, coach, analyst, manager, shoutcaster, referee.
Rules and licences come from the game publisher.
A school league runs weekly matches with student managers and a teacher as sponsor.
Map the roles for a small club.
Build a team that works together.
A support player is added to balance a team after a trial.
A review shows late rotations; two drills fix it.
Sleep, eye breaks, posture and social time.
A 50/10 rule gives a 10-minute break every 50 minutes.
Anti-cheat, no match fixing and no harassment.
A cheater is banned for a season after a review.
Bracket, rules, schedule, tech and referees.
A double-elimination bracket for 16 teams runs in one day.
Costs: prizes, tech, venue and staff.
Break-even is 12 teams at the entry fee.
quiz: Name a role.
Coach, analyst, manager or shoutcaster. (Covered in module 1: The eSports ecosystem. To pass that module: Chart complete.)
Why limit hours?
Protect health and study. (Covered in module 2: Roster and roles. To pass that module: Roles clear.)
Anti-cheat?
Prevents unfair play. (Covered in module 3: Practice and analysis. To pass that module: Three findings.)
Bracket?
Match structure. (Covered in module 4: Wellbeing. To pass that module: Rules clear.)
Break rule?
Regular breaks. (Covered in module 5: Fair play and conduct. To pass that module: Sanctions listed.)
Sponsor rule?
Disclose. (Covered in module 6: Tournament operations. To pass that module: No clashes.)
Break-even?
Teams needed to cover cost. (Covered in module 7: Money and sponsors. To pass that module: Currency shown.)
Review use?
Spot mistakes. (Covered in module 8: Report. To pass that module: Numbers real.)
Sanction?
Penalty for rules breach. (Covered in module 8: Report. To pass that module: Numbers real.)
Equal chance?
No discrimination. (Covered in module 8: Report. To pass that module: Numbers real.)

ladder: The eSports ecosystem

L1: learner can name roles. Focus module: The eSports ecosystem (Understand, 3 h). Know the players, teams, publishers and events. Key points: Roles: player, coach, analyst, manager, shoutcaster, referee. Leagues, tournaments and streams. Rules and licences come from the game publisher. Amateur, school and professional levels.

Teach: open with the worked example. A school league runs weekly matches with student managers and a teacher as sponsor. Then set the activity: Map the roles for a small club. Mark against the standard: Chart complete. Check at this level: Name a role. Model answer: Coach, analyst, manager or shoutcaster.
Roster and roles

L2: learner knows fair play. Focus module: Roster and roles (Apply, 4 h). Build a team that works together. Key points: Skills, in-game roles and communication. Trials and written agreements. Equal chance with no discrimination. Substitutes and rotation.

Teach: open with the worked example. A support player is added to balance a team after a trial. Then set the activity: Build a roster. Mark against the standard: Roles clear. Check at this level: Why limit hours? Model answer: Protect health and study.
Practice and analysis

L3: learner can plan a roster. Focus module: Practice and analysis (Analyse, 4 h). Improve with data. Key points: Review recordings, stats and mistakes. One focus per week. Track win rate and objectives. Give kind feedback.

Teach: open with the worked example. A review shows late rotations; two drills fix it. Then set the activity: Review a match. Mark against the standard: Three findings. Check at this level: Anti-cheat? Model answer: Prevents unfair play.
Wellbeing

L4: learner can run practice. Focus module: Wellbeing (Evaluate, 4 h). Health matters. Key points: Sleep, eye breaks, posture and social time. Limit hours and protect study. Watch for burnout. Know where to get help.

Teach: open with the worked example. A 50/10 rule gives a 10-minute break every 50 minutes. Then set the activity: Write a wellbeing plan. Mark against the standard: Rules clear. Check at this level: Bracket? Model answer: Match structure.
Fair play and conduct

L5: learner can analyse. Focus module: Fair play and conduct (Evaluate, 3 h). Integrity. Key points: Anti-cheat, no match fixing and no harassment. Clear sanctions. Report process. Parents and guardians for minors.

Teach: open with the worked example. A cheater is banned for a season after a review. Then set the activity: Write a code. Mark against the standard: Sanctions listed. Check at this level: Break rule? Model answer: Regular breaks.
Money and sponsors

L6: learner can lead a team. Focus module: Money and sponsors (Analyse, 3 h). Budget. Key points: Costs: prizes, tech, venue and staff. Income: fees and sponsors. Honest sponsor disclosure. Break-even.

Teach: open with the worked example. Break-even is 12 teams at the entry fee. Then set the activity: Build a budget. Mark against the standard: Currency shown. Check at this level: Sponsor rule? Model answer: Disclose.
Report
L7: learner can audit. Focus module: Report (Create, 3 h). Learn. Key points: Results, feedback and costs. Improvements. Share thanks. Plan the next event.

Teach: open with the worked example. Feedback scores 4.5. Then set the activity: Report. Mark against the standard: Numbers real. Check at this level: Break-even? Model answer: Teams needed to cover cost.
